MEMORANDUM

  Agenda Item #: _9_
  Meeting Date: November 5, 2019

TO:  HONORABLE MAYOR AND CITY COUNCIL

THRU:  CAROLYNN PETRU, INTERIM CITY MANAGER

FROM:  KEN RUKAVINA, DIRECTOR OF COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT AND
  PUBLIC WORKS/CITY ENGINEER
  CARL MORITZ, URBAN FORESTER

SUBJECT: CONSIDERATION OF PARKLANDS COMMITTEE RECOMMENDATIONS OF
  OCTOBER 1, 2019

DATE:  NOVEMBER 5, 2019

Issue/Purpose

The purpose of this memorandum is to transmit Parklands Committee recommendation for applications
from the October 1, 2019 meeting to the City Council.

Background/Discussion

At its meeting of October 1, 2019, the Parklands Committee reviewed and discussed four applications
for tree removal or trimming, a past tree removal program in Malaga Cove, and an ad hoc committee to
address parkland encroachments.

1.  PC-518-19; Application to remove 1 Paulownia tree located in the parkway adjacent to 3211
  Rocky Point Road.

  Applicant:  Mark McCalsin
  2120 Paseo Del Mar
  Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

  Staff presented the application to remove a nonconforming Paulownia tree that is blocking the
  view. An additional request was to replace this tree with a varietal that was not the designated
  street tree. The applicant’s representative Allan Rigg spoke in support of removal of the tree and

  1
   replacement with Olive or Forest Pansy trees, along with the owner of 321 Rocky Point Road,
  Kurt Robinson and the adjacent resident of 2105 Paseo Del Mar, Stacy Koehn.

  The committee members agreed the Paulownia tree significantly encroached into the view and
  there is no opposition to removal. The committee understood the parkway frontage on Paseo Del
  Mar was small and a majority of the parkway was adjacent to Rocky Point Road. The committee
  agreed the replacement tree should be planted with the same varietal to provide a consistent design
  and the purple leaves of the Forest Pansy is in character with the purple leaves of the designated
  street tree for Rocky Point Road. They also understood either substitution would require trimming
  in the future to keep below the view.

  Action: Committee member Debra Richie-Bray motioned second by Jeff Groves to
  recommend to the City Council approval to remove 1 Paulownia tree according to the
  ‘Standard Conditions for Tree Removal Approvals’; require $500 payment to the ‘Tree
  Bank’ and removal of the stump; and require 3 Cercis canadensis ‘Forest Pansy’ trees to be
  included in the required landscape plan, to be planted 8 feet from the curb in the parkway
  adjacent to 321 Rocky Point Road after completion of the project. The vote was (5-0 in
  favor).

2.  PC-520-19; Application to remove or top 3 Liquid Ambers tree located in the parkway adjacent
  to 2024 Via Visalia.

  Applicant:  Phillip Kim
  2028 Via Visalia
  Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

  The applicant was at the meeting but didn’t provide comment. One Parklands Committee member
  indicated the farthest tree from the applicant’s home was not in the view. The other members
  agreed but considered trimming three tree to the same height best for the design.

  Action: Committee member Richie-Bray motioned second by Cooper to recommend to the
  City Council approval to top the trees to 26 feet above grade, require annual trimming by
  the applicant with a Tree Topping permit ($475) to maintain safety ant the established view
  line, require the Urban Forester to supervise the initial trimming, and require a Tree
  Trimming permit for all subsequent trimmings. The vote was (5-0, in favor).

3.  PC-521-19; Application to remove of trim down 2 Eucalyptus trees located in the Parklands
  adjacent to 868 Via Del Monte

  Applicant:  Arun Mittal M. D.
  868 Via Del Monte
  Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

  Staff introduced this application for view restoration as a request to remove or trim down 2
  Eucalyptus in the Parklands below, which is adjacent to the Paseo Del Sol fire road. This road is
  actively used for recreation and has very few mature healthy trees left from the 1960’s planting
  due to prolonged drought. Trimming the Eucalyptus by topping is not possible at the level
  requested. Staff recommended thinning the density by 25% and removal of all dead and broken
  branches to increase view through the tree.

  2
   The applicants indicated the trees were barely visible when he built his home 40 years ago and
  they now block his sunset view for part of the year. He indicated he is not in favor of removal but
  as long as the tree are trimmed down to the height of the existing pine trees which would leave
  only trunks.

  The Committee members all agreed that a panoramic view existed that included the Queens
  Necklace and the L. A. Basin lights but a portion of view to the south limited sunset views part
  of the year. Most of the members favored retaining the trees and trimming to improve this view
  through appropriate trimming, not severe topping, as a first step, is preferred to removal.

  Action: Committee member Richie-Bray motioned second by Cooper to recommend to the
  City Council approval of PC-521-19, to trim to remove dead and broken branches and
  reduce density by 25% with no reduction in height, require the applicant to obtain a Tree
  Trimming Permit and the Urban Forester to supervise the initial trimming and all
  subsequent trimmings. The vote was (4-1 in favor, Groves dissenting).

4.  PC-522-19; Application to remove 1 Olive tree located in the parkway adjacent to 2672 Via
  Olivera

  Applicant:  William Shih
  2668 Via Olivera
  Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

  Staff introduced this application as a view enhancement request to remove the Olive tree at the
  adjacent parkway in front of 2672 Via Olivera. His neighbor at this address indicated the Olive
  tree blocked his view also and he supported the application for removal. The resident of 2672
  Via Olivera had requested no replacement tree but indicated he would accept a new tree if required
  by the committee. Staff indicated a new tree could be planted in the parkway closer to the property
  line and more on the level area in the center of the lot.

  The members all agreed the tree blocks the view from both properties and was not a very attractive
  tree that had been trimmed down for the view in the past. The committee did not want to change
  the character of Via Olivera’s Olive tree character but agreed a smaller Olive tree in a different
  location could be maintained below the view from the balcony.

  Action: Committee member Groves motioned second by Richie-Bray to recommend to the
  City Council approval of PC-522-19, to remove 1 Olive tree located in the parkway adjacent
  to 2672 Via Olivera according to the ‘Standard Conditions of Tree Removal Approvals”,
  require $500 payment to the ‘Tree Bank’, removal of the stump, and replacement with a 24-
  inch box designated street tree.

5.  Elm Tree Trimming Program

  Staff brought this question to the committee to clarify what guidelines are to be followed
  concerning the American elm tree trimming program that once existed on Via Media and Via
  Almar. The program is basically obsolete but 9 American elm trees remain, 2 on Via Almar and
  7 on Via Media. The question before the Committee was should this program be re-established

  3
   for the remaining American elm trees and what are the trimming specifications or should trimming
  of the American elm trees for view be governed by the existing Tree Management Policy.

  Action: Committee member Richie-Bray motioned second by Groves to not re-establish the
  American elm tree trimming program and allow the trees to be governed by the existing
  Tree Management Policy.

6.  Discussion for implementing the Policy for Removal of Encroachments in Parklands

  Staff introduced this discussion to provide direction t on how implementation of the existing
  policy for removal of Parkland encroachment should be conducted. The difference between
  rights-of way and Parklands, type of encroachments, existing policies and historical time frames
  for removal were listed. The City Council requested an Ad Hoc committee be appointed to provide
  comments.

  Action: Richie-Bray and Leach volunteered to be on Ad Hoc committee.

Notification

Interested parties attending the Parklands Committee meeting were made aware that the above noted
recommendations would be transmitted to the City Council. This item is also noticed in the standard
manner for City Council meetings.

Alternatives Available to the City Council

City Council has the option to approve, deny, amend or remand this item to the Parklands Committee.
Should the City Council consider amending and have its own hearing on this item, it is recommended
that the discussion be calendared for a future meeting so appropriate notice can be assured.

Recommendation

It is recommended that the City Council review and approve the Parklands Committee recommended
actions of October 1, 2019.
